Clemency

/KLEM-uhn-see/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Clemency means mercy shown by someone in power toward a person who has earned a punishment, softening what they deserve

The judge granted clemency to the first-time offender who had repaid every stolen dollar before sentencing, reducing the term to probation.

Worked Example

The school board showed clemency to the senior who reported his own grading-system prank, cutting the recommended expulsion to a two-week suspension.

The student really was guilty and really could have been expelled. The board's decision to soften the punishment out of mercy — while still acknowledging the wrong — is what clemency means.

How Clemency Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

mercy

mercy: kind treatment of someone you could punish

leniency

leniency: mildness in judging or punishing

compassion

compassion: sympathetic concern for another's suffering

Antonyms

harshness

harshness: severe, unforgiving treatment

severity

severity: strictness in applying full punishment

How Strong Is It? — leniency → clemency → amnesty

leniency vs. clemency

leniency vs. clemency: Leniency is weaker than clemency — it is everyday mildness, like a teacher grading gently, without the weight of an official act of mercy.

amnesty vs. clemency

amnesty vs. clemency: Amnesty is stronger than clemency — it is a sweeping official forgiveness granted to a whole group at once, often erasing offenses entirely.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — clemen-

Root — clemen-: mild, gentle, merciful (Latin clemens)

Suffix — -cy

Suffix — -cy: state or quality of

Put it together

Put it together: Latin clemens meant 'mild, gentle,' and -cy names a state or quality — so clemency is literally 'the quality of mildness': gentleness chosen by someone who had the power to be harsh.

Use the root in a new word: clement

Use the root in a new word: clement: The sailors hoped for clement weather — mild skies from the very root that gives clemency its gentleness toward wrongdoers.

Root Check

Word Choice

Formal

Clemency flows downward from power — a governor, judge, board, or boss softens a punishment that someone genuinely deserves. Keep it distinct from its neighbors in this unit: a reprieve merely delays a punishment without reducing it, and vindication proves the person was never to blame at all. Clemency alone means mercy despite real guilt.
